rounds.title: Baseline — before any of this round's work
rounds.biggestFlaw: Our island is a speck in a huge, uniformly speckled sea. Theirs fills two thirds of the frame and sits in calm deep water with a clean turquoise shelf and a crisp surf collar.
differences: Composition: their island fills the frame; ours is lost in ocean.
Water: theirs is calm with foam only at the shore; ours has white chips everywhere.
Density: theirs is packed with props, fences and crops; ours is sparse.
Light: theirs is warm and directional with readable shadows; ours is flat.
Colour: their greens and sands are vivid; ours are duller and greyer.

rounds.title: Camera, water, terrain, density and light — all five rebuilt
rounds.biggestFlaw: We cast no shadows. Not weak ones, not wrong-angle ones — zero. Four of the five critics named this independently, without seeing each other's verdicts. The reference lays a directional shadow from every flag, fence post, palm frond and 12px stone block; our isolated shed sits on 200px of open sand and touches it nowhere. The result reads as stickers on a blockout rather than a lit scene.
differences: The coast is a 3-4 block cliff of flat untextured sand dropping straight into the sea. Theirs is a low one-block lip meeting the water almost at sea level, with a wet-sand band behind the surf collar.
Every interior surface is empty. The whole decoration budget is welded around the coastline as a hedge of palms; step inland and it is bare slabs.
Broken style and scale consistency — flat-shaded low-poly palm fronds next to voxel rocks, at a visibly coarser texel density.
The buildings crowd into a band across the top-right, leaving large empty plots dead in the bottom-left.
Deep-water local contrast averages 2.25 against their 20.04 — but this directly contradicts the water builder's own measurement and is not being acted on until resolved.

pieces.biggestGap: Open ocean has no sun glitter past the shallow ring — deep-water contrast 2.25 vs their 20.04. CONTESTED: the builder measured the reference's open water as having ZERO pixels above L=200 and removed the glitter deliberately. Two measurements of the same pixels disagree; resolving that comes before either is acted on.
No cast shadows on the ground at all, and 8-12px grey blotch noise on the sand swinging 25 levels where the reference is one clean flat value.
Not one standing prop on any grass cell or sand plaza inside the island. All decoration is a hedge around the coast.
Zero cast shadows. Measured off their flag: a point at screen-height H drops its shadow ~0.68H, and lit sand (225,211,180) lands at (167,163,142) in shadow — a 25% multiply, not a grey overlay.

rounds.title: Shadows, a real beach, and the water contradiction settled
rounds.biggestFlaw: Our shadows are too SHORT to read. The sun was 15.3 degrees off the camera axis, so every shadow fell behind the object throwing it — the map was never broken. The azimuth is now solved off their flag (0.68H against their measured 0.68H) and shadows exist, but the judge still sees 'a flat sticker of objects hovering on a beige plane'. The reference's shadows are long and soft; ours are short and hard.
differences: FRAMING REGRESSION: the island now runs off the bottom of frame and crops the moored ship at the left edge. Round 1's silhouette fit was correct; the coast rebuild moved it.
The right third collapses into an unreadable brown-and-orange mass — no negative space, no separation between market and shipyard.
Four unrelated architectural vocabularies on one island: a curved-roof pagoda, a half-timbered northern house, a Mediterranean cottage and pirate rigging. This is asset selection, not rendering.
Our ocean reads as a tiling noise pattern rather than water — flat lighter-blue rectangles at even density.

SETTLED: the water contradiction. Both sides were partly right. The reference's sea is TWO materials split by screen height plus a sun lane confined to one corner. The builder was right to delete the glitter field and wrong to delete the lane with it — our white chip tier is 13.7x short in the near-field right lane.

pieces.biggestGap: Shadows are cast correctly now but read short. Shadowed-sand share is 18.2% against the reference's 8.3% — we have twice their shadow AREA at the right multiply and bearing, but ours lands on palm canopies shadowing other palm canopies instead of on open plaza. The gap here is composition, not light.
Rebuilt from a 21px single cliff to three low bands ending 0.24 units above the water, with a wet-sand ring. Measured against their 11px wall.
Add the white chip tier to the near-field lane only: reference runs 4.9% of pixels above L=200 there, we run 0.36%.
